evidence_class: layout construction and a comparison by P4's own methods: the stability, balance, trim and rotation numbers have the evidence class of P4 (partly independent of Stage 1); the weights of the added length are Raymer's statistical equations as ratios plus an assumed shaft weight; the drag and hours are Stage 1's build-up and mission with changed wetted areas (a coding check, not a measurement)

extension.what_moves: the last fuselage control station, the spinner and the propeller plane; nothing ahead of the engine bay's end
extension.length_rule: the least length that puts the rearmost point of either tail inside the disc's radius the P4 clearance (1.0 ft) ahead of the propeller plane; never negative
extension.fuselage_weight: Raymer (15.49), p. 404, as a ratio on r0's fuselage weight: wetted area (Stage 1's plus the loft's added skin) to the 1.086, tail arm to the -0.051, length over diameter to the -0.072
extension.flight_controls_weight: Raymer (15.54), p. 404, as a ratio on r0's weight: fuselage length to the 1.536. It is charged although the tail does not move aft with the propeller, because the equation is in fuselage length; this counts against the lengthened layouts
extension.added_weight_station: the added fuselage weight and the shaft are put at the middle of the added length (aft of r0's fuselage end by half the extension); the flight controls stay at r0's station

shaft_lb_per_ft.source: An assumption, not a number from a source. Raymer p. 221 says only that an offset of more than a few inches needs a drive shaft with its own bearing support, and gives no weight; no open weight for such a shaft was found. The low end is about a bare steel tube: the record's 450 shp at the ledger's 2,030 rpm is a torque of about 1,164 lb ft, and a 3 in tube of 0.058 in wall in 4130 steel weighs about 1.8 lb/ft (computed in the record with Raymer (14.45), p. 388, and Table 14.3, p. 366-367, taken from the library's chapter notes; the page could not be opened in this session, so that tube is support and not a test target). The value and the high end add couplings, a bearing and its support frame every few feet. The trade is repeated at both band ends.

shaft_tube_for_support.note: 4130 steel tubing as the chapter notes of Raymer Table 14.3 give it; support only

candidates.A: PD-20 as P4 recorded it: no extension, tails forward with straight trailing edges, areas grown to keep the volume coefficients
candidates.B: r0's tail planforms (unswept tailplane leading edge), areas and arm; the aft fuselage lengthened by the length rule
candidates.Bs: as B with straight trailing edges on both tails (PD-20's item 1), which needs a shorter extension: the smallest extension that clears the disc at r0's tail arm and areas
candidates.C: straight trailing edges, the tail arm between PD-20's and r0's that gives the least empty-weight change among the arms whose payload-on rows all pass; volume coefficients kept
candidates.placement: every candidate: wing by P4's rule (mean static margin 0.10, independent neutral point), main wheels by the 15 deg tipback rule, nose wheel at r0's station

drag_and_hours.method: P3's own route (prelim/p3_loft.buildup_with_loft_areas): Stage 1's build-up and mission on the built aircraft with wetted areas changed and nothing else. Tails: Stage 1's wetted-area rule on the new areas. Fuselage: Stage 1's area plus the loft's added skin. Form factors, interference factors and reference lengths stay Stage 1's (a longer body has a lower form factor, which is not credited)
drag_and_hours.cases: hours on station on r0's fuel (a) at r0's take-off weight with the layout's wetted areas, the number the task names, and (b) with the take-off weight also raised by the layout's empty-weight change. (b) is the number the selection rule uses

selection_rule.pool: A, B and every row of the arm scan (Bs and C are rows of it)
steps: 1. A layout stays only if every payload-on row passes: R13 at the full-fuel and empty-fuel centre of gravity (row 1); every payload-on loading inside the envelope (row 3); nose-wheel load of every payload-on loading inside 5 to 20 % (row 4); tail lift at rotation within the limit of 1.0; trim within its limit; overturn angle at most 63 deg; propeller ground clearance at rotation at least 9 in; both tails at least 1.0 ft ahead of the propeller plane inside the disc.

2. If any layout left also passes rows 3 and 4 with the payload off and no ballast, only those stay. If none does, payload-off ballast does not rank the layouts: it is reported for each and becomes an operating limit of the chosen one (PD-13).

3. Of those left, the one with the most hours on station on r0's fuel, with its wetted areas and with the take-off weight raised by its empty-weight change (case b). Weight and drag both act on R5, so one number carries both.
4. Layouts within 0.01 h of the best count as tied; the tie goes to the least empty-weight change.
5. If no layout passes step 1, nothing is chosen and the trade goes to the owner.
selection_rule.sensitivity: the whole trade is repeated with the shaft at 2 and at 10 lb/ft; the report says whether the choice changes
not_ranked_but_reported: tailplane root leading edge behind the wing root trailing edge
empty-weight change (it enters step 3 through the weight, and step 4)

balance.h_cg_ft_note: The centre of gravity is on the fuselage reference line, as in Stage 1.

neutral_point.downstream_rule: linear from 0 at the root trailing edge to d(alpha_h)/d(alpha) at the tail's quarter mean chord, then constant to the end of the fuselage
neutral_point.bodies: The fuselage only. The sponsons lie inside the wing chord, where Multhopp's d(beta)/d(alpha) is 0, so (3.7) gives them nothing; Multhopp's nacelle term (3.10) is not applied. The turret and spinner are left out.
neutral_point.propeller_downwash_slope: the tail's d(alpha_h)/d(alpha) from the lattice is used at the propeller too (the hub is inside the lattice's wake sheet, where the lattice cannot be evaluated)
neutral_point.blade_for_side_force_factor: the P6 representative blade (PD-18): chords at 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 R and the blade angle at 0.75 R of each point from runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p6/p6.json. P6 failed its validation row 5; only the blade's geometry and pitch are taken from it, and the power-on rows carry no verdict.

airfoil_cm0.source: P2 record runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p2b/p2.json (section moment about the quarter chord, NACA 4415 measured); the ledger has -0.08

propeller_clearance_ft.source: Least distance, along the axis, from the propeller plane forward to any part of a tail surface inside the propeller disc's radius. A judgement: the library gives no number (Raymer p. 222-223 says only that a propeller behind a wing should be mounted as far behind it as possible). 1 ft is about 0.15 propeller diameters and leaves room for the blades' deflection and the elevator's trailing edge. Solved at the band ends as a sensitivity

r1.tail_volume_coefficients: kept: horizontal c_ht times r0's ht_volume_scale, vertical c_vt (Raymer (6.28), (6.29), p. 111); the areas grow as the arm shortens. Aspect ratios and tapers kept.
r1.tail_trailing_edges: straight (all the taper on the leading edge), both tails. Added on 2026-11-27 after a trial of the methods, before any recorded run: with r0's planforms the solution does not exist (PD-20). The first form is still solved in the record.
r1.wing_position_rule: Stage 1's own rule: the mean of the full-fuel and empty-fuel static margins (payload on, gear up, nominal empty weight) is 0.10 MAC, the middle of R13, here with the independent neutral point, power off.
r1.main_gear_rule: Stage 1's own rule: the main wheels are the tipback angle (15 deg) behind the aftmost centre of gravity with the gear down (Raymer p. 232). The nose wheel stays at r0's station.
r1.weights: Tail weights by Raymer (15.47) and (15.48) (area to the 0.896 and 0.873; the tailplane's quarter-chord sweep terms; the fin weighed unswept, as Stage 1 weighs r0's) and the fuselage by the tail-arm term of (15.49) (L_t^-0.051), as ratios on r0's component weights, p. 404; nothing else changes and the aircraft is not re-sized (the take-off weight moves by the same pounds).

findings_for_r1: Layout for r1 (PD-21): Bs = arm scan row 10 (tail arm 13.577 ft). Tail arm 13.577 ft, tailplane 135.48 ft^2, fin 37.08 ft^2, trailing edges straight; wing leading edge at the root at 10.082 ft (+0.918 ft from r0); main wheels at 14.895 ft; nose wheel unchanged.
Aft fuselage for r1: lengthened by 1.976 ft to 30.559 ft; the propeller plane moves to 30.709 ft; the engine stays at r0's station and a shaft of that added length carries the propeller.

Weights for r1, as changes on r0 (not re-sized): horizontal tail -0.10 lb, fuselage +20.09 lb, flight controls +7.16 lb (the fuselage figure includes 9.88 lb of shaft at an assumed 5 lb/ft); empty weight +27.15 lb against +26.93 lb for PD-20.

Drag and hours: wetted area +12.89 ft^2, CD0 +0.000145, hours on station -0.042 h at r0's weight and fuel and -0.158 h with the empty-weight change in the take-off weight (PD-20: -0.309 and -0.423 h).

Rows on the chosen layout: static margin 0.1010 full and 0.0990 empty; 0 of 132 payload-on loadings outside the envelope; nose-wheel load 13.6 to 15.1 %; tail lift at rotation 0.928 of the limit (PD-20: 0.986); propeller ground clearance at rotation 12.10 in (PD-20: 15.88 in; at least 9 in).

Payload off: 132 of 132 loadings are outside the envelope on the chosen layout, and on every other layout of the trade. The aftmost payload-off centre of gravity is +0.263 ft from the main wheels (positive: behind). Flight without the payload needs 474 lb of ballast at the payload station to bring every payload-off loading to the aft limit (428 lb by P4's figure, which takes the aftmost loading only; 46 lb only to bring the centre of gravity to the wheels); with it 0 of 132 loadings are outside the envelope. PD-20 needs 465 lb (420 lb by P4's figure). This is an operating limit for P8 (PD-13).

Moving the main wheels does not remove the ballast: it is the aft limit of R13 that the payload-off loadings break. With the wheels moved to 17.399 ft for payload-off tipback, the tail would need 2.434 of its limit at rotation.
Tail and wing: the tailplane is 0.501 of the wing area with its root leading edge 3.85 ft behind the wing's root trailing edge (PD-20: 0.611 and 1.06 ft).

The shaft weight is an assumption (5 lb/ft, band 2 to 10). At the band ends the rule chooses: 2 lb/ft: Bs = C = arm scan row 10 (tail arm 13.577 ft); 10 lb/ft: Bs = arm scan row 10 (tail arm 13.577 ft).

For r1 and P9, not answered here: Stage 1 needs the fuselage extension, the tail arm and the tails' leading-edge sweep as inputs; the shaft, its bearings and its critical speed are not designed; the tail roots sit on a slender tail cone whose structure is not sized; the form factor and the skin-friction length of the longer body are Stage 1's unchanged; the open items of P4 (sponson, tail roots on the engine bay) stand.
